For these questions, you must make the construction lines otherwise your answer may not be registered.
Also, your browser may ask whether you want to "leave the page". In this case, you should click leave and your answer will be saved.


(a) By moving the red points in the diagram below, place the blue line so that is a perpendicular bisector to the black line.


[[jsxgraph width="600px" height="400px" input-ref-ans1="sR1" input-ref-ans2="sR2" input-ref-ans3="sR3" input-ref-ans4="sR4" input-ref-ans5="sR5" input-ref-ans6="sR6" input-ref-ans7="sR7" input-ref-ans8="sR8" input-ref-ans9="sR9"]] // Create board var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingBox:[-6,4,6,-4], showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false, keepaspectratio:true }); // Create immovable reference line var refLine = board.create("segment", [[-2,0], [2,0]], { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black" }) // Construct movable points var pointStyle = { showInfoBox:false, withLabel:false }; var cenA = board.create("point", [-4.5,2.75], pointStyle); var radA = board.create("point", [-3.5,2.75], pointStyle); var cenB = board.create("point", [-2,2.75], pointStyle); var radB = board.create("point", [-1,2.75], pointStyle); var linePoint1 = board.create("point", [-4.5,1.25], pointStyle); var linePoint2 = board.create("point", [-2,1.25], pointStyle); // From movable points form constructing tools var circleA = board.create("circle", [cenA, radA], { dash:1 }); var circleB = board.create("circle", [cenB, radB], { dash:1 }); var constLine = board.create("segment", [linePoint1, linePoint2]); // Points implied by students construction var circInter1 = board.create("intersection", [circleA, circleB, 0], { visible:false, showInfoBox:false }); var circInter2 = board.create("intersection", [circleA, circleB, 1], { visible:false, showInfoBox:false }); var lineInter = board.create("intersection", [refLine, constLine], { visible:false, showInfoBox:false }); // Points needed to check validity of student line stack_jxg.bind_point(sR1, lineInter); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR2, linePoint1); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR3, linePoint2); // Points needed to check student's construction stack_jxg.bind_point(sR4, cenA); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR5, cenB); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR6, radA); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR7, radB); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR8, circInter1); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR9, circInter2); board.unsuspendUpdate(); (b) By moving the red points in the diagram below, place the blue line so that it bisects the acute angle between the two black lines.


[[jsxgraph width="600px" height="400px" input-ref-ans10="sR10" input-ref-ans11="sR11" input-ref-ans12="sR12" input-ref-ans13="sR13" input-ref-ans14="sR14" input-ref-ans15="sR15" input-ref-ans16="sR16" input-ref-ans17="sR17" input-ref-ans18="sR18" input-ref-ans19="sR19"]] // Create board var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingBox:[-6,4,5,-4], showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false, keepaspectratio:true }); // Create immovable reference lines var fixedPoint = board.create("point", [-2,0], { fixed:true, showInfoBox:false, visible:false }); var refLine1 = board.create("segment", [fixedPoint, [2,-1.5]], { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black" }) var refLine2 = board.create("segment", [fixedPoint, [3,3]], { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black" }) // Construct movable points var pointStyle = { showInfoBox:false, withLabel:false }; var cenA = board.create("point", [-4.5,2.75], pointStyle); var radA = board.create("point", [-3.5,2.75], pointStyle); var cenB = board.create("point", [-2,2.75], pointStyle); var radB = board.create("point", [-1,2.75], pointStyle); var radC = board.create("point", [-1.5,0], pointStyle); var movLinePoint = board.create("point", [-3,0], pointStyle); // From movable points form constructing tools var circleA = board.create("circle", [cenA, radA], { dash:1 }); var circleB = board.create("circle", [cenB, radB], { dash:1 }); var circleC = board.create("circle", [fixedPoint, radC], { dash:1 }); var constLine = board.create("segment", [fixedPoint, movLinePoint]); // Points implied by students contruction var circLineInter1 = board.create("intersection", [circleC, refLine1], { visible:false, showInfoBox:false }); var circLineInter2 = board.create("intersection", [circleC, refLine2], { visible:false, showInfoBox:false }); var circCircInter1 = board.create("intersection", [circleA, circleB, 0], { visible:false, showInfoBox:false }); var circCircInter2 = board.create("intersection", [circleA, circleB, 1], { visible:false, showInfoBox:false }); // Point needed to check validity of student line stack_jxg.bind_point(sR10, movLinePoint); // Points moved by student for construction stack_jxg.bind_point(sR11, cenA); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR12, cenB); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR13, radA); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR14, radB); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR15, radC); // Implied points formed by students construction stack_jxg.bind_point(sR16, circLineInter1); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR17, circLineInter2); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR18, circCircInter1); stack_jxg.bind_point(sR19, circCircInter2); board.unsuspendUpdate(); [[/jsxgraph]]

falsefeedback.text: The line you have constructed is not sufficiently close to a perpendicular bisector of the black line:

truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

There are three steps to constructing the perpendicular bisector of a line:

(1) Construct two circles centred at each end of the black line.

(2) Ensure the radii of the circles are the same and greater than half the length of the black line. The easiest way to achieve this is to place the points on the radii at the opposite ends of the black line to their respective centres.

(3) Place the perpendicular bisector so that it passes through both of the intersection points of the circles.


Here is what your finished construction should look like:

[[jsxgraph width="300px" height="200px"]] // Create board var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingBox:[-6,4,6,-4], showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false, keepaspectratio:true }); // Create immovable reference line var refLine = board.create("segment", [[-2,0], [2,0]], { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black" }) // Construct points in correct positions var pointStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false visible:false, showInfoBox:false, withLabel:false }; var cenA = board.create("point", [-2,0], pointStyle); var radA = board.create("point", [2,0], pointStyle); var cenB = board.create("point", [2,0], pointStyle); var radB = board.create("point", [-2,0], pointStyle); var linePoint1 = board.create("point", [0,sqrt(12)], pointStyle); var linePoint2 = board.create("point", [0,-sqrt(12)], pointStyle); // From points form constructing tools var circleStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, dash:1 }; var circleA = board.create("circle", [cenA, radA], circleStyle); var circleB = board.create("circle", [cenB, radB], circleStyle); var constLine = board.create("segment", [linePoint1, linePoint2], { fixed:true, highlight:false }); [[/jsxgraph]]
You have correctly placed the centres of each circle at the ends of the line.

falsefeedback.text: You have not placed the centres of each circle sufficiently close to the ends of the line.

truefeedback.text: You have correctly constructed circles of equal radii.

falsefeedback.text: You have not created circles with sufficiently equal radii. To do this, you should ensure each circle passes through the centre point of the other.

truefeedback.text: You have correctly placed the points of your line on the intersections between the two circles.

falsefeedback.text: You have not placed the points of your line sufficiently close to the intersections between the two circles.
The line you have constructed is not sufficiently close to a bisector of the angle between the black lines:

truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

There are four steps to constructing the bisector of an angle:

(1) Construct a circle centred at the intersection of the lines which forms the angle. This is done for you, but it is helpful to make the circle larger for a more accurate bisector.

(2) Construct two additional circles which are centred at the intersections between the first circle and the black lines.

(3) Ensure the radii of the additional two circles are the same and large enough for the circles to intersect. The easiest way to achieve this is to place the points on the radii at the intersection between the black lines.

(4) Place the perpendicular bisector so that it passes through the intersection points of the two circles.


Here is what your finished construction should look like:

[[jsxgraph width="300px" height="200px"]] // Create board var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard("jxgbox", { boundingBox:[-6,4,6,-4], showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false, keepaspectratio:true }); // Create immovable reference lines var fixedPoint = board.create("point", [-2,0], { fixed:true, showInfoBox:false, visible:false }); var refLine1 = board.create("segment", [fixedPoint, [2,-1.5]], { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black" }) var refLine2 = board.create("segment", [fixedPoint, [3,3]], { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black" }) // Construct fixed points in the correct positions var pointStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false visible:false, showInfoBox:false, withLabel:false }; var cenA = board.create("point", [sqrt(34)*(5/17)-2, sqrt(34)*(3/17)], pointStyle); var radA = board.create("point", [-2,0], pointStyle); var cenB = board.create("point", [sqrt(73)*(16/73)-2, -sqrt(73)*(6/73)], pointStyle); var radB = board.create("point", [-2,0], pointStyle); var radC = board.create("point", [0,0], pointStyle); var movLinePoint = board.create("point", [sqrt(34)*(5/17)+sqrt(73)*(16/73)-2, sqrt(34)*(3/17)-sqrt(73)*(6/73)], pointStyle); // From points form constructing tools var circleStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, dash:1 }; var circleA = board.create("circle", [cenA, radA], circleStyle); var circleB = board.create("circle", [cenB, radB], circleStyle); var circleC = board.create("circle", [fixedPoint, radC],circleStyle); var constLine = board.create("segment", [fixedPoint, movLinePoint]); [[/jsxgraph]]
You have correctly placed the centres of each movable circle at the intersections of the immovable circle and the black lines.

truefeedback.text: You have correctly constructed circles of equal radii.

falsefeedback.text: You have not created circles with sufficiently equal radii. To do this, you should ensure each circle passes through the centre point of the other or the intersection of the two black lines.

truefeedback.text: You have correctly placed the your line such that is passes through the intersections between the two circles.

falsefeedback.text: You have not placed the your line such that it passes sufficiently close to the intersections between the two circles.
